headline: Kazakhstan's Snow Leopards Make Stunning Recovery
meta_description: Kazakhstan's snow leopard population has nearly doubled since the mid-1990s, thanks to conservation efforts and a new nature park.
summary_short: From fewer than 100 to nearly 190: Kazakhstan's snow leopards stage a remarkable comeback after decades of dedicated conservation work.
body:
Kazakhstan's snow leopard population has nearly doubled over the past three decades, climbing from 80–100 individuals in the mid-1990s to 152–189 today. This dramatic recovery represents one of the region's most significant conservation successes, driven by sustained effort and a new nature park created this year.

The turnaround reflects the power of long-term commitment. Decades of conservation work have stabilized a species that once faced steady decline across Central Asia. The establishment of the new nature park signals renewed momentum, providing protected habitat in the mountain regions these elusive cats call home.

While challenges remain for snow leopard populations across their broader range, Kazakhstan's numbers offer real hope. The story shows that endangered species can recover when communities and governments work together to preserve them.
